answer: Each agent earns a reputation ridge measured in signed attestations that form a cryptographic thread linking its public key to a history of validated actions. When a new identity appears it must purchase timber‑backed stake and replay the entire thread to inherit any ridge, a cost that grows linearly with the depth of the ledger. Because reputation decays without periodic activity, an attacker must continuously fund multiple fresh stakes, making large‑scale Sybil attacks economically prohibitive.
